reconstructed_theorem_text: Let T be a first-countable topological space, Omega a measurable space, and E a topological measurable space whose open sets are measurable. Let mu be a probability measure on Omega and X:T x Omega -> E such that X(t,.) is measurable for every t. Suppose that for mu-almost every omega the entire map t -> X(t,omega) is continuous on T. Then the map t -> (X(t,.))_*mu is continuous from T into ProbabilityMeasure E, with its standard weak topology. The supplied elaboration identifies the hidden map as precisely the pushforward by X(t,.).
objects: First-countable topological parameter space T; measurable sample space Omega; topological measurable state space E with OpensMeasurableSpace.
Probability measure mu and parameterized random variables X(t,.).
Marginal laws rho(t)=ProbabilityMeasure.map mu (X(t,.)), using hX(t) to supply the a.e.-measurability proof.
domains: t ranges over arbitrary T, not necessarily a real interval or ordered time set.
omega ranges over Omega and X(t,omega) lies in E.
The law curve has codomain ProbabilityMeasure E with its standard weak topology, characterized by bounded continuous real test functions.
quantifiers: For every t, X(t,.) is measurable.
For mu-almost every omega, the whole function t -> X(t,omega) is continuous.
The resulting law map is continuous at every parameter point.
assumptions: E is topological and measurable with all open sets measurable; BorelSpace equality, metric structure, compactness and separability are not assumed.
Measurability of each slice and a single AE path-continuity assertion; no joint measurability hypothesis is present.
conclusion: Continuity of t -> rho(t) in the usual topology of probability measures.
The hidden application mu.map is genuinely the marginal pushforward by X(t,.), as explicitly supplied in the approved context.
scopes: The AE quantifier precedes the global Continuous predicate, giving one full-measure set of continuous paths.
This differs from separate continuity at each t with t-dependent exceptional sets.
No path regularity is asserted for every omega, and no Wasserstein or total-variation continuity is asserted.
constant_dependencies: No constants, bounds, exponents or existential quantitative witnesses occur.
